patch_description: All prior attempts score ~0.18 (min_area_normalized ≈ 0.006), far below the ~0.031 benchmark. They rely on slow softmin gradient ascent that gets stuck in symmetric ring configurations where small triangles persist. This rewrite uses a completely different paradigm: fast vectorized evaluation of the exact objective (min triangle area / hull area) plus basin-hopping stochastic hill climbing. Each move perturbs one point; the move is accepted only if the true (non-smoothed) objective improves. Adaptive step sizes plus repeated perturbation-restart (basin hopping) from multiple deterministic seeds escape the poor symmetric local optima that plague gradient methods. Since the exact objective is evaluated directly (not a soft approximation), progress is never lost to smoothing bias. The convex hull of the final configuration is rescaled to unit area, which only helps (interior points stay inside, hull area becomes exactly 1).
